result.title: Lifecycle | Opire Docs
sentences: Each creator reviews the solution and, if it meets the issue requirements, arranges payment for their own bounty.
Claiming a bounty never creates an automatic payment.
result.excerpt: document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme","dark"),document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme-choice","dark"),function(){try{const c=new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).entries();for(var[t,e]of c)if(t.startsWith("docusaurus-data-")){var a=t.replace("docusaurus-data-","data-");document.documentElement.setAttribute(a,e)}}catch(t){}}()Skip to main contentOpireGitHubDiscordEnglishEnglishEspañolPortugueseFrançaisDeutsch简体中文OverviewIntroductionUse casesGetting startedInstall botCommandsRewardsIntroductionCosts & paymentsLifecycleTipsIntroductionLifecycleFAQOn this pageLifecycle At Opire, the lifecycle of a bounty begins when a code owner wants to incentivize the resolution of an issue in their repository. They create a bounty using our commands or the web platform. Upon creating the bounty, it will appear on the Opire platform, as well as on the issue itself. Any programmer can view the bounty and decide whether to attempt to resolve the issue, notifying others using the try command. Once the developer opens a pull request (PR) with the necessary changes, they can claim the bounties associated with the issue. This notifies each bounty creator with a link to the PR. Each creator reviews the solution and, if it meets the issue requirements, arranges payment for their own bounty. Claiming a bounty never creates an automatic payment. Multiple Bounties​ An issue can have more than one bounty created by its code owners. If a code owner prefers to start with a more modest amount, they can add another bounty later. These are added to the existing total, and each creator remains responsible only for the bounties they created. Multiple Creators​ Multiple code owners of the same repository may create bounties for the same issue. In that case, the amount the programmer receives is the sum of those bounties. Each creator pays their part separately.Edit this pagePreviousCosts & paymentsNextTipsMultiple BountiesMultiple CreatorsOpire

Minimum amounts​ ContributionMinimumCreated forBounty$20 USDResolving a GitHub issueTip$1 USDThanking a contributor on an issue or pull request Only code owners can create bounties, and only for issues in their own repositories. More than one code owner may create a bounty for the same issue; each person is responsible only for the bounty they created. When a bounty is paid​ Creating or claiming a bounty does not create an automatic payment. A developer submits a pull request, then each bounty creator reviews whether it meets the requirements described in the issue. If it does, that creator arranges payment for their own bounty. Opire publishes and tracks bounties and claims; payments are arranged directly by the people involved. Check the issue requirements and agree on any payment details before you create or claim a bounty. Tips​ Tips are not tied to resolving an issue. Create one only when you want to thank a specific contributor. Like bounties, a tip is not an automatic platform payment; the sender and recipient arrange payment directly.
